decisions.quote: Discrete emotions may affect memory above and beyond such dimensions, with recent research indicating that disgusting information is better remembered than frightening information. We initially sought to determine whether participants are sensitive to the effects of discrete emotions when predicting their future memory performance. Participants in Experiment 1 were more confident in their memory for emotional (both frightening and disgusting) images relative to neutral images, but confidence did not differ between frightening and disgusting images. However, because we did not replicate the mnemonic advantage of disgust, subsequent experiments were concerned with testing the replicability of this effect.
decisions.reason: Parent independently read the complete available current abstract and preserved acquisition history. Three actual experiments retest disgust-versus-fear recall, but no original author, title, year or reference list is printed. The sole shipped Chapman2017 paper fits the topic; a shared generic finding does not independently establish that this is its exact original or exclude another disgust-memory report. Publisher access failed and the linked OSF contains data rather than the article. Retain actual original-identity access limit; do not infer a genuine omission or certify represented identity from the shipped entry alone.

rejected_expert_certainty.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this work. The blind coder recorded a single target (target_index 0) for the retested mnemonic advantage of disgusting over frightening images, leaving the citation fields blank solely because the available primary source text is an abstract that describes the retested finding without printing the in-text citation. Shipped row input_row_index 1800 (Chapman, 2017, 'Enhanced recall of disgusting relative to frightening photographs is not due to organisation', doi 10.1080/02699931.2017.1394817) already represents this exact target finding for this replication paper, and there is no evidence of an additional unrepresented original.
